evidence:
Observed on 2026-09-17 on branch `fix/fault-receive-registers`, based on
`29fb847938b1054aaa2f1bd616ac2d3ee1f0744e`. The tested implementation was
uncommitted; its `slime-root` tree identity is
`06bd5fb09b9ecd7d4c5f906dba670272767562f1540c5c1fd04205c61ab8e31f`,
computed by the system-image closure resolver. The base commit alone does not
contain this repair.

Both receive wrappers now synchronize the valid returned fast-register prefix
into the same receive buffer before service decoding. The explicit wrapper does
not acquire the ambient buffer; the ambient wrapper reacquires it only after
receive completes. Long fault payload tails remain kernel-written and intact,
even when service decoding rejects their length.

`just test_sel4_root` passed 264/264 tests across 21 modules. New tests preload
stale words and verify fresh VM-fault instruction, address, access and status;
cover lengths 0, 1, 3, 4, 5 and 8 with unchanged tail/unrelated storage; and
preserve service capability-transfer refusals. An independent read-only review
traced the pinned receive/fault APIs and found no blocking introduced defect.

The existing twenty-incarnation private-memory cycles workload retains ten clean
exits and ten deliberate VM faults. Its odd cycles now alternate guard stores
and instruction fetches from already backed private large frames. Each target
observed five Write faults at `0x08000000` (the end of its 16384-page private
window) and five Execute faults at `0x04000000` (inside that backed window).
The checker joins each fault to a distinct task, installed quota/base, preceding
full growth and cycle report. ARM Write/Execute status values were respectively
2480242758/2181038094; RV64 values were 7/1. Neither target reported stale zero
status or address 9. Reclamation/reuse checks remained intact.

| RV64 QEMU, 3072 MiB | `43dd3549849cf3e24b2a1ebfc4f4ac933155c5c2cd482e3ea30e319a3a8569c0` | `b29b253c8a025e05abfc76a33738782e0b8a8af2c14d8e207d72a857d85ce82c` |

The ARM closure identity is
`5388cae3417c3fc0f443946d6174f9e3e208a4d297b3d78900b67a0da0bdb7e9`.
Raw serial captures are local ignored artifacts at
`build/private-memory-cycles-qemu-arm-virt.serial.log` and
`build/private-memory-cycles-qemu-riscv-virt.serial.log`; these hashes do not
assert remote archive retention. Both lanes used the pinned one-CPU QEMU profile.

Final sequential verification passed: `just test_sel4_root`,
`just fmt_check_all`, `just lint_all`, `just ruff`,
`just sel4_root_boot_check`, the root-boot checker's `--platform qemu-riscv-virt`
run, `just private_memory_check`, `just private_memory_cycles_check`,
`just sel4_fault_check`, `just sel4_gate_control_check`, `just docs_check` and
`just tasks_check`. Image closures and dependent test-run identities were
regenerated before these runtime checks. Gate controls rejected 1856 mutations,
including eight new wrong-task/access/status/address, missing/duplicate-fault,
NX-at-guard and missing-backed-region controls; eight image-identity and four
runtime controls also passed.

This repairs fault payload attribution and qualifies the specified 64 MiB
private-memory fault cases on QEMU. It does not close MEM-1G, qualify 256 MiB
isolation, or make a physical-machine claim. The pre-existing MEM-1G and other
working-tree drafts were retained in stash
`68cc9df8a7187ab37b205b0dd1359e3d1446e914` before this clean-base repair.
